answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can earn reputation or submit work, then slash that stake when independently verified audits catch fraud. Splitting one agent into a hundred aliases does not multiply influence: each alias must fund its own bond, and rewards are weighted by bonded capital rather than account count. A pigment-marked kernel can help auditors trace a comet of linked submissions, but the defense rests on the bond; the attacker pays real capital and risks losing it for every Sybil identity.
